title: Trump meets love interest at Mogilevich's Moscow hotel
description_short: Trump meets love interest at Mogilevich's Moscow hotel
description_medium: Donald Trump reportedly attended a party at Moscow’s Baltschug-Kempinski hotel during a November 1996 trip. A biographical account places the gathering in a venue called “The Library.”
description_long: A biographical account places Donald Trump at a party in Moscow’s Baltschug-Kempinski hotel during an early November 1996 trip. The gathering was reportedly held in a room called “The Library.” The same account links the hotel to Semion Mogilevich and associates the trip with a romantic relationship, but neither the ownership claim nor the personal connection is independently established. A later Senate Intelligence Committee report examined Trump’s contacts and business interests involving Russia, but does not establish details of this hotel anecdote. The reported party is distinct from the ownership and relationship claims. Neither hotel ownership at the time nor a romantic connection has been independently verified.

title: Trump: ICE deports 3 U.S. citizen children to Honduras
description_short: Trump: ICE deports 3 U.S. citizen children to Honduras
description_medium: In April 2025, immigration authorities deported three U.S. citizen children from Louisiana to Honduras alongside their mothers. The children belonged to two families: two sisters, ages four and seven, were citizens while their mother had a deportation order; a two-year-old in another family was also a citizen. The cases raised urgent questions about how citizenship claims were handled during removal proceedings.
description_long: In April 2025, three U.S. citizen children from Louisiana were deported to Honduras with their mothers. The children were part of two families removed on consecutive days. In one case, a mother had a deportation order while her daughters, ages four and seven, were U.S. citizens; the younger child was reported to have cancer. In the second case, the mother and older daughter had deportation orders, while the two-year-old daughter was a U.S. citizen. The cases drew attention to how immigration enforcement handled children’s citizenship and family unity during removals. The legal circumstances differed between the families, as did the children’s ages and the orders against their mothers. The circumstances prompted questions about how citizenship claims were verified and how the children came to travel with their mothers.
notes: The individual family records and parents’ accounts are needed to clarify consent, citizenship documentation and the removal process in each case.

title: Trump: RFK vaccine advisors lie about flu vaccine amid vote
description_short: Trump: RFK vaccine advisors lie about flu vaccine amid vote
description_medium: The Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices voted on June 26, 2025 to recommend single-dose influenza vaccines without thimerosal for children, pregnant women, and other adults. The linked timeline places the votes after Robert F. Kennedy Jr. replaced the committee's membership. The discussion centered on a preservative and allegations about its safety.
description_long: On June 26, 2025, the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices voted to recommend single-dose influenza vaccines without thimerosal for children, pregnant women and other adults. The meeting took place after Robert F. Kennedy Jr. replaced the committee’s membership. Kennedy ally Lyn Redwood presented claims about the preservative, and a CDC document containing contrary information was removed shortly before the meeting. Committee member Robert Malone said the document lacked approval from the secretary’s office. Thimerosal was present in only a small share of flu vaccines, and established evidence did not support claims that it causes autism. The vote concerned the composition of recommended vaccines; it did not end influenza vaccination. Claims made during the presentation were not established evidence of harm. The committee’s votes and the safety claims raised during the meeting were separate parts of the discussion. Thimerosal is a preservative used in some multidose vaccine vials.

title: Trump: Guccifer 2.0 goes public, launches DCLeaks and sends DNC docs to online media
description_short: Trump: Guccifer 2.0 goes public, launches DCLeaks and sends DNC docs to online media
description_medium: The Guccifer 2.0 persona distributed stolen Democratic National Committee documents to journalists during the 2016 campaign. U.S. intelligence later attributed the operation to Russia’s military intelligence service and linked its activity to DCLeaks and WikiLeaks. The operation used a purported independent hacker identity to publicize material obtained through an intrusion into Democratic organizations.
description_long: The Guccifer 2.0 persona distributed stolen Democratic National Committee documents to journalists during the 2016 election campaign. U.S. intelligence later attributed the operation to Russia’s military intelligence service and described related promotion of DCLeaks and WikiLeaks. The persona contacted reporters and presented itself as an independent Romanian hacker. It also sent documents marked confidential to William Bastone of The Smoking Gun and claimed responsibility for hacking the DNC. DCLeaks published documents before WikiLeaks released a larger batch in July. These distribution channels combined the theft of information with efforts to attract news coverage and shape how the material reached the public. The persona’s claimed Romanian identity differed from the later U.S. intelligence attribution to Russian military intelligence. The event concerns dissemination of the stolen material; it does not establish how individual voters responded or measure an effect on the election result.

title: Trump's FBI labels Black protesters a terrorist threat, then admits they found nothing
description_short: Trump's FBI labels Black protesters a terrorist threat, then admits they found nothing
description_medium: An FBI report dated August 3, 2017, used the label “Black Identity Extremists” for a purported domestic terrorism threat. Former officials and legal experts criticized the designation as unsupported and warned of civil-rights implications. The FBI later stopped using the term and said it had identified no murder committed by a Black activist group.
description_long: An FBI report dated August 3, 2017, used the label “Black Identity Extremists” to describe a purported domestic terrorism threat. Former officials and legal experts criticized the designation as unsupported and warned that it could affect civil rights. The label drew concern because it appeared to group political activism under a security category without identifying a coherent movement. A former senior counterterrorism official questioned the basis for the classification and raised privacy concerns. The report emerged shortly before the deadly white supremacist rally in Charlottesville, sharpening criticism about how threats were framed. The FBI later stopped using the term, and later officials said they could identify no murder committed by a Black activist group. Those later developments are distinct from the original report. The FBI’s use of the designation raised concerns about surveillance and the treatment of Black political activity.

title: Trump Tower Russia Meeting: Don Jr., Kushner, Manafort Met for Dirt on Clinton
description_short: Trump Tower Russia Meeting: Don Jr., Kushner, Manafort Met for Dirt on Clinton
description_medium: On June 9, 2016, Donald Trump Jr., Jared Kushner and Paul Manafort met Russian nationals at Trump Tower after an email offered damaging information on Hillary Clinton as Russian-government support for Donald Trump's campaign. Trump Jr. replied, “I love it.” The meeting later drew scrutiny in the Mueller investigation.
description_long: On June 9, 2016, Donald Trump Jr., Jared Kushner and campaign chairman Paul Manafort met at Trump Tower with Russian nationals, including Natalia Veselnitskaya. Emails arranging the meeting described an offer of damaging information on Hillary Clinton as part of Russia’s support for Donald Trump’s campaign; Trump Jr. replied, “I love it.” The meeting later became a focus of Special Counsel Robert Mueller’s investigation into possible coordination between the campaign and Russia. Trump Jr. later described the meeting publicly as concerning adoptions. The episode raised questions about accepting foreign assistance in a U.S. election. The emails do not by themselves establish that the offered material was delivered or that a crime occurred. The meeting’s political significance exceeded what the correspondence alone establishes about criminal liability. The emails became public during the campaign and prompted congressional scrutiny of foreign contacts with U.S. political campaigns.

title: Trump: FBI raids Rudy Giuliani, retrieves Victoria Toensing's phone for Ukraine investigation
description_short: Trump: FBI raids Rudy Giuliani, retrieves Victoria Toensing's phone for Ukraine investigation
description_medium: On April 28, 2021, FBI agents searched Rudy Giuliani's home and office and took Victoria Toensing's phone as part of a Justice Department investigation into Giuliani's Ukraine dealings. The search was an investigative step, not a finding of guilt. The investigation concerned his 2019 dealings in Ukraine.
description_long: On April 28, 2021, FBI agents searched Rudy Giuliani’s home and office and took a cellphone belonging to his attorney, Victoria Toensing, as part of a Justice Department investigation into Giuliani’s activities in Ukraine. The Associated Press reported that agents executed search warrants as prosecutors examined whether Giuliani had unlawfully represented Ukrainian interests or lobbied U.S. officials on behalf of clients. The inquiry concerned his dealings during 2019, when he was acting as Donald Trump’s personal lawyer and seeking information about Ukraine. A search warrant is an investigative step, not a finding of guilt. Giuliani’s role as a prominent Trump ally and his Ukraine work drew attention during the first impeachment inquiry. The search therefore connected a criminal investigation of a presidential lawyer’s activities to a politically consequential period in U.S.-Ukraine relations, while leaving questions of liability for the legal process to resolve.
